transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Williams, thank you for coming back in to see me today. I need to talk to you about your son's visit yesterday. There was a mistake made with his vaccinations.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: When we were preparing the shots, we used a weight band for an older, heavier child instead of his actual weight. This means he received a dose of one of the vaccines that was higher than what he should have had.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You gave my baby too much medicine? Are you kidding me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am very sorry. This was our mistake, and I take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My son is tiny! How does that even happen? Who was checking the dose? Was it you?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, I was the one who drew the medication. I didn't double-check the weight chart before preparing the dose. I can see how scary and frustrating this is for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Scary? I'm terrified! He's my baby! Do you have any idea what this does to him? I can't be dealing with this, I have two jobs, I can't be spending my whole week in a hospital because you can't read a chart!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand you're feeling overwhelmed with everything on your plate right now, but we need to focus on the—

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Don't tell me what I'm feeling! You're the one who messed up! Is he going to be okay or not?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: To make sure I've explained this clearly, do you understand that he got a higher dose than recommended for his weight?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I get it! He got too much! Now tell me if he's poisoned or something!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There is no evidence that this dose will cause long-term harm, but we need to be proactive. I've already consulted with the toxicology team and the pediatric chief.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So you're just guessing he's fine?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, based on the specific vaccine, the overage is within a range that we can monitor safely. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if any of this makes sense! This is completely unacceptable!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I completely agree. It shouldn't have happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care that you agree! I want to know what happens now!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, so here is the plan. First, I want you to bring him back tomorrow morning at 9:00 AM for a physical exam and a blood test to check his kidney function. I have already scheduled that appointment for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't just leave work whenever I want!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I realize that's a huge burden. I will personally call your employer if a medical note helps, or we can move it to 7:00 AM to get him in before your shift. Which works better?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Seven is better, but I'm still furious.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. In addition to that visit, I want you to monitor his temperature and feeding patterns every four hours today. I'm going to give you a specific checklist to track this. If you see any rash or a fever over 101, you call my direct line immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What if he has a reaction tonight? I can't just wait until seven tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You won't have to. Here is my personal cell phone number and the direct line to the on-call pediatric resident. If anything happens, you bypass the front desk and call us directly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And how do I know this won't happen again? How do I trust you with my kids?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is a fair question. To prevent this, I have already met with my supervisor to implement a new "double-sign" policy in our clinic. From now on, two clinicians must sign off on the weight band and the dose before any vaccine is administered. I am also undergoing a retraining module on medication safety this week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You should be.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I agree that I should be. I've also entered a formal incident report into the hospital system so this is documented and tracked.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just can't believe this. I'm so stressed as it is.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is the last thing you needed on top of everything else. Look, I have to go see another patient now, so let's wrap up the logistics.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait, you're just leaving?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I just want to make sure you have my number and the 7:00 AM appointment is set. I'll be the one seeing you tomorrow morning. We will go over the blood results together as soon as they come in, likely by noon tomorrow. Does that timeline work for you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine. I'll be here at seven.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you. I'll see you then.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language at the end ('let's wrap up the logistics') and interrupts the patient's emotional expression at 01:21 ('I understand... but we need to focus on the—').

E.justification: Error named in first turn, lay language used, comprehension checked twice (01:38 and 02:10), and no false reassurance given.

A.justification: Direct apology used ('I am very sorry'), resident takes full personal responsibility, and maintains accountability despite patient pushback.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('scary and frustrating', 'overwhelmed') and references the patient's specific life stressors (two jobs).

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps (blood test, monitoring), timelines (7:00 AM, every four hours), patient role (checklist), and prevention (double-sign policy).
